column1: # Anchor tasks — the 88 modules from ANCHORS.tsv that face outside and are not
# anchored yet. Generated 2026-08-01. Read ANCHORS.tsv's header first.
# THE JOB: move the expected values in the tests from "we wrote them, from our
# own reading of the spec" to "they came from outside". The foreign tool
# normally runs ONCE, at capture time; the bytes it produced are committed as
# literals and the test stays offline, deterministic and dependency-free.
# SOURCE   VECTOR:<where>  published byte-level vectors covering the gap
#          CLI:<tool>      a command-line tool can emit or check the bytes
#          DAEMON:<tool>   needs a service standing up — much dearer
#          CAPTURE:<where> real artifacts obtainable from a public source
#          NONE            nothing external exists; a legitimate end state
# COST     S  drop in published vectors, or re-run a harness THAT ALREADY
#             EXISTS here with a different input
#          M  build a harness around a CLI, or transcribe a vector set
#          L  stand up a daemon/toolchain, or write a foreign-format parser
#          -  SOURCE is NONE, nothing to do
# ⚠ TWO TRAPS, both already paid for once in this repo:
#   1. Do NOT close one of these by un-skipping a live test into the default
#      gate. Capture the bytes once, commit them, keep the test offline. A
#      flake in the gate costs more than the anchor is worth (see cba13a4).
#   2. NEVER compute a "vector" from our own output. An open, labelled gap is
#      strictly better than a fake anchor.
# ⚠ THIS IS A LOWER BOUND. Classification is per module, so a module that is
#   EXTERNAL overall can still have one uncovered path inside it — enip is
#   EXTERNAL (goldens captured from cpppo/pycomm3) yet its symbolic-segment
#   pad byte is never exercised, because the one captured sample has an
#   even-length tag name. Those per-path gaps are not counted here.

The default PRG IS now fixed-key AES (prg.Aes128Mmo) and it did NOT buy byte-exact agreement with Google: that would additionally need Google's own fixed keys, tweak convention, control-bit extraction, packed value-correction and protobuf key layout, and their tests compute expectations inline rather than publishing a vector file. So the earlier note's central claim was WRONG - the PRG was never the only obstacle. What the swap did buy is ~25-36x speed (SPEC.md §'PRG choice'). Tier stays REDERIVED and the vectors were NOT regenerated: they are stated over the retained Sha256Prg instantiation, and DpfWith shares one body of correction-word code, so they still pin the construction byte-exact. Genuinely external and newly added, but narrow: the MMO step is pinned to FIPS-197 App. B - that anchors the AES call, NOT the DPF.

column7: CLOSED 2026-08-02: ran our own setup+prove for the module's existing nt fixture (harness_test.zig's 4-constraint/3-public-input circuit, fixed toxic waste + r,s), exported it through a new snarkjs_export.zig (JSON shape reverse-engineered from snarkjs@0.7.6's own bundled source: decimal-string field elements, G1=[x,y,"1"], G2=[[c0,c1],[c0,c1],["1","0"]] MATH order), and ran a REAL snarkjs@0.7.6 (fetched via bunx, Apache-2.0, never vendored) against it. Literal `bunx snarkjs groth16 verify ...` crashed on THIS host (Bun's web-worker shim SIGILLs spawning ffjavascript's WASM thread pool — a Bun/npm-package interop bug, reproduces for ANY input, confirmed unrelated to our data); invoking the SAME unmodified snarkjs@0.7.6 groth16.verify with its own documented single-thread fallback forced on (process.browser=true; delete globalThis.Worker — a condition its own source already branches on, not a patch) worked: RESULT true, exit 0, on the FIRST correctly-invoked try — no serialization deviation found. A one-limb-tampered copy (pi_a.x+1) got RESULT false, exit 1, confirming the oracle has teeth. Frozen as literals in snarkjs_kat_test.zig (JSON text + transcript), re-derivable (not hand-transcribed) since the fixture's toxic waste/r/s are small fixed integers. What this does NOT anchor: QAP/R1CS correctness (snarkjs never saw our R1CS — only the final group elements) — that layer has no external oracle for a custom circuit and stays self-checked (qap.checkDivisible == r1cs.isSatisfied), which is a legitimate end state, not remaining debt.
